# Production Frame Investigation Plan

**Goal:** Refresh full-frame Alkaid/W26 measurements on the actual production bundle after the CPU optimizations, then select the next bottleneck from evidence.
**Base:** 49148fae5a22aaf953faadfd13bc3ac2b7e384b3.
**Scope:** Existing authorized audit item 16. Diagnostic code is external to the application bundle, loaded into a fresh browser context. No change to application quality or rendering configuration.

- [x] Build the unchanged application in production mode with the existing Yandex S3 configuration and /titan-engine-dev/ base. Record source revision and hashes of the exact served bundle.
- [x] Access existing production module exports and DI bindings; do not rebuild a second runtime or rely on minified class names. Native Chrome/AMD, 1280x720, DPR1, same belt cameras for Alkaid and W26.
- [x] Measure three minimally instrumented 240-frame stationary/moving windows per scene, following warmup. Capture intervals and CPU renderFrame; no GPU queries, per-draw hooks or profiler in these windows. Movement is a fixed 3990-km/360-degree trajectory by frame index, not fixed velocity.
- [x] Separate 240-frame GPU whole-frame, per-pass and per-volume-draw windows. Defer GPU query polling until measurement has stopped; fail on disjoint/context loss. Preserve per-frame correspondence and raw samples. CPU component/profile windows are separate from baseline cadence.
- [x] Check native renderer, completed sample counts, pending bake work, all console/assets diagnostics, scene screenshots, exact bundle hashes and restored wrappers/camera. Analyze CPU stalls, GPU bottlenecks and p95/p99. Do not sum medians or claim before/after FPS from these current-state measurements.
- [ ] Record findings and the next evidence-based target in docs/project-audit-2026-10-21.md and a versioned JSON archive. One independent final review of the evidence. Local commit on existing audit branch, no push. If investigation finds a bounded actionable defect, define its regression/paired validation before changing production code.

The earlier real-cloud soak covered short repeated transitions; long-term heap/VRAM analysis is a separate follow-up, not claimed by this frame profile. Source-only changes are absent in this investigation, so fresh typecheck/build and harness/provenance checks are required; rerunning unchanged application unit/browser suites is unnecessary unless a production fix is made.

Execution: build/typecheck passed (Vite 9.91s). First smoke ASI defect preserved and fixed in the external probe; second smoke passed five modes. Full run completed 26 windows/6240 frames, 576 cloud responses, no console/assets errors/warnings/aborts. Both screenshots viewed. Thirty-two evidence hashes plus the 32-file build manifest and every reported summary/sample count verified. Archive/audit written; independent review and local commit remain. The first next target is RenderPass asteroid draws and explicit MSAA blit timing. No production change chosen; Three's OculusBrowser depth invalidation makes a blind resolveDepthBuffer toggle nonportable, while no actual resolve cost has yet been measured.

steps: Use an isolated checkout of base. npm ci; restore the embedded diagnostic sources to their recorded paths. Do not execute against a dirty application checkout.
Set VITE_FS_DRIVER=s3, VITE_S3_URL=https://storage.yandexcloud.net, VITE_FILE_BUCKET=textures, VITE_SHOW_STATS_PANEL=false, VITE_SKY_SOURCE=gaia. Run npm run build -- --base=/titan-engine-dev/.

Run node benchmark-results/heavy-scenes/run-production-frame-2026-10-27.mjs --smoke, then without --smoke, sequentially on native Chrome. Filenames are exclusive: use a fresh workspace/results directory; do not overwrite historical outputs.

The runner freezes dist, verifies its manifest before and after, imports only retained production exports and uses the existing DI token identities. Exact historical build checksums are recorded; timestamps/cloud data/device can change new results.

For original local evidence run node benchmark-results/heavy-scenes/archive-production-frame-2026-10-27.mjs --verify. This verifies original raw hashes, summaries and local bundle; newly rerun timings have different hashes.

scope: Current-state diagnosis, not a before/after improvement. Native headless Chrome on one AMD/ANGLE D3D11 device, one dense global-belt viewpoint per scene. Cloud models/textures fetched normally, but their individual response bytes were not archived.

Plain windows record renderFrame entry intervals and wall durations with a small wrapper; these are not screen presentation timestamps or direct GPU utilization. Short/long interval alternation makes 1000/p50 misleading as FPS.

Movement is 2 TU (~3990.52 km) plus 360 degree yaw in 240 frame-indexed steps, not fixed real-time velocity. Simulation time continues, windows run in a fixed sequence, and cache/thermal/order effects are not controlled for before/after comparison.

GPU modes run separately; elapsed scopes include command execution and may include submission gaps. Per-draw scopes omit surrounding renderer work, clears and MSAA resolves. Do not add medians, subtract cross-window medians as exact overhead, or compare instrumented cadence as FPS.

CPU components nest and may include driver stalls. CDP spans measure() setup/cleanup as well as frames: idle, getError and snapshot getParameter samples outside the measured frames must not be treated as application-frame hotspots. No getParameter calls were intercepted inside either CPU frame window.
Large CPU wall spikes from some plain windows did not recur in the separate CPU diagnostic windows. Their cause remains unlocalized; no tail-latency fix is claimed.

The sourceModuleRequests guard matches root /src, /@vite, /@id and /tests paths, not every possible base-prefixed source path. The unchanged production bundle manifest and reviewed built-module-only probe are the primary evidence that no dev runtime was loaded.

Screenshots and complete production output stay in ignored local artifacts and are indexed by SHA256; they are not embedded in this JSON. Diagnostic sources, raw measured samples, CPU profiles and logs are embedded. No visual-equivalence or full-scene coverage claim is made.
Menu resource counts reset after both scenes, but this ~11-minute run is not a long heap/VRAM leak or GC-normalized memory test. JS heap snapshots are not comparable retained memory measurements.

Three 0.182.0 resolves multisampled targets after renderer.render. resolveDepthBuffer=false is not a portable preserve-depth control: in its OculusBrowser invalidation branch it invalidates read and draw depth attachments. This branch is not active on the recorded Chrome. No resolve policy was changed and no redundant-resolve cost or speedup is proven.

nextTarget.first: Measure individual asteroid material draws within RenderPass and gl.blitFramebuffer MSAA resolves in separate native GPU windows; attribute actual cost before changing the renderer.
nextTarget.subsequent: Select a bounded optimization from those measurements, then require paired baseline/candidate samples and depth/HDR image regression checks with MSAA 0/4 before retaining it. Dust/nebula raymarch and reconstruction fallback remain measured hotspots.
outstanding: Localize rare plain-window long frames with targeted tracing while preserving a plain cadence control
Long repeated scene transitions with GC-normalized heap and resource/VRAM evidence

review.scope: Two staged documentation/evidence files; fresh read-only final review with no children or heavy reruns
review.assessment: Approved bounded diagnostic stage; no material deviations or corrections required
review.reviewCoverage: Complete probe, runner, archive verifier, staged audit, selected raw/derived evidence, relevant engine/rendering source and lightweight integrity checks. Audit numbers independently recalculated. No independent screenshot opening or fault injection.
declinedToJudge: Cross-device or interactive presentation FPS: single-device headless render-entry profile
Before/after speedup: no paired candidate; simulation, order, caches and thermal conditions uncontrolled
Cause of large plain-window CPU spikes: separate CPU diagnostic did not reproduce them
Pure shader execution versus submission gaps inside elapsed GPU query scopes
Exact overhead from subtracting separate GPU-window medians
Individual asteroid-material and MSAA-resolve cost, not separately measured
Safety or benefit of disabling depth resolve, no runtime candidate or equivalence proof
Long-term heap/VRAM leak freedom from a short run and menu counters
Visual equivalence/full-scene coverage; reviewer did not independently open screenshots
Bit-identical future cloud reproduction, remote response bytes not archived
Comprehensive source-request detection, root-only guard has disclosed limits
General-purpose harness fault tolerance beyond reviewed setup/timeouts/queries/cleanup/runner failure paths; no injected context loss/restoration/filesystem failures
Fresh application regression-suite health, unchanged suites not rerun
Final review metadata and commit correctness, executor steps after review
rulings: Accept the stated device/headless scope. Keep intervals as render-entry timings; make no screen FPS or cross-device claim. Interactive presentation may differ.
Accept diagnosis only. A future optimization must use paired baseline/candidate runs; this sequence cannot establish a speedup or causality.
Keep spike localization open under audit item 16. The absence of spikes in the diagnostic window does not exonerate any subsystem or show a fix.
Keep elapsed-scope terminology and its submission-gap caveat. No pure shader busy time or utilization claim is derived from these queries.
Reject that subtraction as a cost estimate. Only same-frame nonnested draw sums are aggregated before quantiles; separately measure missing resolve/renderer scopes next.
Accept as the next bounded measurement target, not a defect or promised gain. Record actual material calls and blits before deciding on production code.
Keep flags unchanged. Any future resolve change requires depth/HDR parity and portable handling of the documented OculusBrowser invalidation path, plus measured benefit.
Keep long-duration memory/VRAM work open. Resource-counter reset is useful evidence only for the observed teardown; heap retention and driver memory remain unproven.

Accept executor visual inspection and recorded hashes only. The viewed scenes show expected dense belts/nebulae; no image equivalence, close-view coverage or independent reviewer visual validation is claimed.

Accept reproducibility limits explicitly: exact historical cloud bytes are unavailable. Preserve inputs, source revision, local build hashes and raw results; future cloud/device/timing variation is expected.

Accept built-output and reviewed import provenance as primary evidence for this run. A future general-purpose runner should also record base-prefixed source requests; the current guard is not described as comprehensive.

Keep the temporary diagnostic scope. Actual successful run and reviewed failure/cleanup paths support these measurements; injected exceptional paths are not certified and failed future runs must not be accepted as evidence.

Accept no redundant application-suite rerun for unchanged source. Fresh typecheck/build, native smoke/profile and integrity checks passed; prior unit/browser results are not relabeled as newly executed.

Executor verifies both reviewed file hashes before metadata edits, preserves copies, permits only review/provenance/timestamp additions in the archive and an appended audit conclusion, verifies again, and commits exactly the two documentation files locally without pushing.
